public_comment.topic: Displeasure that the capital plan is used as a funding source -- unexpended project money returned to free cash rather than staying committed to the projects voted at town meeting

minutes.headline: School department pulls back its capital request; committee plans to finalize FY27 priorities by mid-December
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee heard the facilities department's FY27-29 (and outyear) requests -- a large TCP re-roofing figure, public safety building roof/flooring/HVAC/boiler replacements, TCP asbestos abatement, and Fitzgerald Field regrading -- while the chair reported the school department is revising its own capital request after superintendent concerns about accuracy, and the track and field project is being routed to a separate spring town meeting article instead of this cycle. The committee set a schedule (Dec 3, 10, 17) to compile and vote a preliminary FY27 priority list, treating it as subject to revision once free cash and budget numbers firm up in January.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call, all members voted I)

budget_items.what_was_said: Chair explained that once town meeting authorizes a capital list, unspent or cancelled project funds can only be reappropriated to another project or closed out to free cash -- neither requires new town meeting authorization. Three FY22 projects had remaining funds or were not going forward.

Money previously appropriated for a TCP roof section (the now-decommissioned section) was evaluated for reallocation to another TCP roof section but that was found not to make sense and would create a patchwork job.

budget_items.topic: TCP re-roofing of the non-decommissioned section
budget_items.what_was_said: A large re-roofing figure appears in the outyear list for the section of TCP that is not being decommissioned; the chair flagged it as a number everyone should understand and a big future discussion item.
The FY29 column showed a small figure on the TCP roof line that appears to have been copied down in error from the row above; Ruth agreed to correct it.

Ruth said he applies a contingency to most of his estimates since many are based on prior-year cost-per-square-foot figures; the town manager noted contingency practice has not been consistent across all department heads and should be reviewed.

Estimate covers full replacement of both boilers plus oil transfer pumps; burners were already replaced once in 2008 and are failing again, and the contractor recommended full replacement rather than burners-only given the building cannot be shut down and runs on oil.

Request covers removing asbestos flooring, hard ceilings and pipe insulation from the decommissioned section of TCP; an extra amount was added for demolition to reach asbestos in concealed pipe spaces. Debate over whether to fund it now or bundle it with a future decision on the building's fate.

budget_items.topic: Fitzgerald Field regrading, reseeding and fencing
budget_items.what_was_said: Covers bringing in fill material, engineering for drainage/grading, initial fertilizer program, and fencing repairs (shared with a town beach fencing fix); a member questioned whether the field's actual usage justifies the cost.

A member raised concern about bundling an unrelated town beach fencing fix into the Fitzgerald Field request; it was noted the town beach portion came in smaller than expected and could be pulled out and covered by the parks operating budget instead.

budget_items.topic: Free cash certification timing vs. capital prioritization
budget_items.what_was_said: The Town Manager noted free cash has not yet been certified, raising the question of how much available funding should factor into prioritizing the list versus a pure prioritization exercise; the chair said the committee's main task is the priority list regardless.

A member suggested the committee should start considering whether some requests could use alternative funding sources like Chapter 90 or borrowing rather than the general capital fund, which could change what gets prioritized above the line.

Considering moving prior TCP roof appropriation to a different TCP roof section
transfers.outcome: discussed only, not pursued -- would have created a patchwork roof

decisions.decision: Committee to aim for meetings on December 3, 10 and 17 to build and finalize a preliminary FY27 capital priority list.
The December recommendation will be treated as an initial/preliminary list subject to revision in January as budget and free-cash numbers become clearer.
The committee will still meet on December 10 but push the actual prioritization vote to December 17 to accommodate a member's absence.
The Turkey Hill track and field project will not be part of this capital planning cycle; it is expected to come forward as a separate article at spring town meeting.

The school department is expected to redisuss and potentially revise its capital plan request at its own committee meeting the same night, after concerns were raised about the accuracy of figures presented to Capital Planning.
Committee agreed to start factoring alternative funding sources (e.g., Chapter 90, borrowing) into how it evaluates and prioritizes requests.
Ruth agreed to correct the erroneous $40,000 figure on the TCP roof line in the FY29 column of the shared spreadsheet.
Town Manager to follow up with the minutes clerk about a backlog of unapproved Capital Planning Committee minutes.
